short: Four men held the throne within eighteen months, exposing that legions, not birth, now made emperors.
full:
Nero's suicide on 9 June 68 CE left no heir from Augustus's line, and the throne fell to whoever commanded enough legions. Galba, governor of Spain, was acclaimed first but murdered by the Praetorian Guard in January 69 CE in favour of Otho, who himself lost the field to Vitellius's Rhine army at the first battle of Bedriacum that April and took his own life.

Vitellius held Rome only until the eastern legions proclaimed their own commander, Vespasian, who took the city after further fighting and was recognised by the Senate on 21 December 69 CE. The year proved that an emperor no longer needed senatorial or dynastic legitimacy, only the loyalty of an army — a lesson provincial legions would act on again whenever the centre showed weakness. Vespasian's victory founded the Flavian dynasty and restored a fragile stability.
